_help.about: Sports: rare genetic abnormalities any plant can carry (design 29 Sept 2026, Mike: 'each plant should also have rare sport forms which are like a unique and rare genetic abnormality'). PlantGenetics rolls each plant once, from its position (the same plant is the same sport on every visit), at its shape's rate; which kind it is is weighted toward what's documented in its genus (by_genus, researched: named cultivars that arose as sports, wild abnormal forms) and, for the Amorphophallus, in its species (the catalogue's cycle.sports). Clonal plants (tuber offsets, stolons, bulbils: the aroids that make them) roll per clump, so a sport shows as a whole clump, as it does in nature. Restart after editing.
_help.kinds: Every kind: code (the engine's number, packed into the plant's instance data with its moss: moss + 2 x code), label (what the HUD calls it after the name), size (height multiplier), look (what it looks like), inherit (how it passes to offspring in a cross: seed = seed_share of the seedlings; recessive = seed_share, all of them if both parents carry it; clonal = only offsets and cuttings, seed_share of seedlings; ploidy = the ploidy rules below), fertility (seed set when it's a parent), shows (what the engine draws today; form sports are recorded for the mesh builders).
_help.by_shape: The chance a plant is a sport (rate: one in 1/rate) and the kinds its shape class can show, weight 1 each. Grasses, tussocks, mosses, cushions, mats and knees don't sport (nothing to see). 'aroid' is every species with a cycle block (the Amorphophallus).
_help.weights: Kind weights: shape default, genus documented, species documented; a kind documented in the genus or species is allowed even if the shape list lacks it.
_help.ploidy: Crosses: 2x x 2x gives 2x, with an unreduced gamete now and then (unreduced: that share of seedlings are 3x, a quarter as many 4x — the rare spontaneous polyploid); 4x x 4x gives 4x; 2x x 4x gives 3x (triploid: seed set x triploid_fertility); an apomictic mother's seed is her clone.
_help.by_genus: Researched per genus (agent pass, 29 Sept 2026; 217 of 469 genera have a documented sport): kind and a documented example.
